## Source: amazon-inspector (62ef2123979b9b0569b31e090e1b575bc392c7e40aa1367eed178147b4931c4c)
setup.py defines a custom install cmdclass (PostInstall) that runs on `pip install` and collects installer-side identifiers — hostname, USER/USERNAME, current working directory, VIRTUAL_ENV, and CI-related environment variables — and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded interactsh collector at https://dbq1g44hj5j25tbieep0dmbhfakw1pyzc.oast.fun/humbility-shared, with an accompanying DNS prefetch of a package-named subdomain under the same canary host. The destination is not the installer's infrastructure and is not caller-configurable; the behavior is undisclosed and fires automatically from the sdist build on a default install when no matching wheel is available, and the shipped wheel installs the same package tree. The name and shape are consistent with a dependency-confusion canary squatting an internal package name on public PyPI to fingerprint build systems that resolve the public name instead of the intended private one.

## Source: kam193 (bad6120ea5f69f851eafe78dfbb832979077fa6c0175c2bdda88bf073b8ad487)
Installing the package or importing the module exfiltrates basic information about the host, and the package has no other purpose.
